# Cedric Stanhope

## Overview

- **Age:** Ten to eleven years old during volume 1; around thirteen in volume 2; sixteen in volume 3  <sub>[v1 c26 P4](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0004), [v1 c26 P12](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0012), [v2 c1 P46](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0046), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c23 P28](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0028)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v2 c23 P28](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0028)</sub>
- **Origin:** United States (Boston)  <sub>[v2 c23 P9](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0009)</sub>
- **Role:** School student  <sub>[v2 c5 P5](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

Cedric is described as a remarkably attractive and delicate boy with a round, small face, fine and exquisite features, and a complexion resembling a flower. He has deep, dark-blue eyes and a halo of chestnut curls, which he later cuts short by the age of sixteen. He is initially small for his age, with slender hands and an expressive, responsive smile that illuminates his whole countenance.

_Sources: [v1 c5 P5](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0005), [v1 c19 P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077), [v1 c23 P4](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0004), [v2 c15 P8](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0008), [v2 c23 P28](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0028)_

## Personality

Cedric is a thoughtful, sensitive, and imaginative child who possesses a quiet, reflective nature and deep artistic sensibility. He is polite, courteous, and polite to others, defending younger students at school and demonstrating an intuitive understanding of the feelings of those around him. Though imaginative and given to rich fantasies, he is also surprisingly brave, manly, and capable of holding his own in physical fights and games.

_Sources: [v1 c5 P5](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0005), [v1 c18 P31](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0031), [v1 c18 P35](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0035), [v2 c5 P20](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0020), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038)_

- Vivid imagination
- Thoughtful and introspective  <sub>[v1 c18 P28](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0028)</sub>

- To grow tall and strong like his father  <sub>[v1 c18 P37](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0037), [v2 c23 P28](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0028)</sub>

## History

Cedric arrives in Brierley from Boston to reside with his grandmother, Mrs. Stanhope. On his first day at Brierley school, he instantly bonds with the new schoolteacher, Nell Harcourt, after sharing a silent, understanding smile with her. He soon becomes her favorite pupil and a close friend, frequently bringing her wild orchids and sharing his imaginative stories about 'rock people'. During a winter night when Posy Fay falls ill with croup, Cedric's quick action is not needed, but he continues to attend school diligently and bonds with his classmates, even engaging in a physical fight with St. Clair Trask to defend the honor of the American flag. Over the years, Cedric grows taller and becomes a protective figure for the younger schoolboys. When his father, Stephen Stanhope, visits Brierley and later marries Miss Rosalind Penrose, Cedric welcomes Rosalind warmly into his life. Following their wedding, Cedric prepares to return to Boston to live with his father and stepmother.

_Sources: [v1 c5 P5](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0005), [v1 c5 P20](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0020), [v1 c18 P28](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0028), [v1 c18 P31](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0031), [v1 c18 P33](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0033), [v1 c23 P28](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0028), [v2 c23 P28](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0028)_

## Background by volume

- Born in the United States as the son of Stephen Stanhope  <sub>[v1 c18 P10](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0010)</sub>
- Lost his mother at a young age, whom he deeply cherished  <sub>[v1 c18 P28](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0028), [v1 c19 P24](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0024)</sub>
- Sent from Boston to Brierley to live with his grandmother

## Quotes

> I ask you to take these, teacher, which I discovered in the field belonging to Mr. Duckett, and I returned so I could offer them to you since I believed you were a lady who would appreciate them, and also because . . . teacher, I am fond of you.  <sub>[v1 c15 P20](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0020)</sub>

> You see, teacher, I didn't know I was going to be an orphan until father told me, and then I felt very sorry for myself.  <sub>[v1 c18 P28](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0028)</sub>

> I was sure father could be relied upon to choose a lovely little second mother for me. Teacher, it is wonderful to possess a father you can rely on.  <sub>[v1 c29 P1](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0001)</sub>
